context: Checkpoint 2026-08-03. The declared-node-base slice is implemented and proven. The node resolved declarations from wherever it was started while already carrying --refarm-dir; SOVEREIGN_BASE now joins SOVEREIGN_DIR as an injected selector, all seven Group A+B sites read it, and the selectors travel to the operation child so it stops admitting an operation from one directory and refusing it from another. Proven in the exact broken scenario: daemon restarted from the repository, authenticated POST /operations returned exitCode 0, succeeded, 10 packages, 0 issues, where the same directory previously gave exit 1 and invalid-or-missing-operation-result. D4 landed too — `refarm doctor` now names the directory, reporting auth-policy and config divergence as warnings, silent when there is nothing local to diverge; this node shows two findings from the repository and none from home. Three existing guards corrected the implementation along the way and each was right: injected_vars must carry only what the operator declared, enrolment may not import the config package, and a JS package's hand-written .d.ts must declare a new export or only type-check sees it.
